requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: A single exact root cron entry for 02:15 daily was installed, crond was enabled and running, and both the schedule and service remained healthy after reboot. Repairing the malformed, non-executable prepared command was a necessary prerequisite to making the scheduled invocation functional.
Direct executions appended output to the requested log. The initial record survived reboot, and a second post-reboot execution increased the log to two records, demonstrating append-mode retention.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and bounded outage, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered crond, schedule, executable, and persisted/appended log data.
limitations: No naturally scheduler-triggered execution at 02:15 was captured; timing is established by the exact active cron entry, while command and append behavior were tested manually.
Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on Alpine, although crond health was directly checked through OpenRC before and after restart.
No separate cluster-state probe was applicable to this single standalone node; recovered task service and data state were directly demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: The command repair, cron configuration, crond enablement, bounded log tests, and reboot were causally connected to the task or mandatory restart protocol. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/inventory-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present after execution; it was small and low risk but not cleaned up. No package-health regression or unsafe new listener was observed.
